notes: PUBLISHED FOR EARLY TESTING ONLY: this circuit is unreviewed, AI-generated code. The crate's planned expert security review (sha256_var/mso_splice/onehot_cursor/digest_id_extract, plus a known ECDSA range-check gap) has not landed. Do not treat as vouched-for or production-ready; do not rely on it for real relying-party trust decisions. | Fixes a real under-constraint found while scoping that review: digest_id_extract's value-byte mapping is right-aligned, so for CBOR uint length classes 0/1/2 the high-order bytes of the exposed digestID were free witness variables, and both range checks went vacuous (gated by a different class's selector). A prover generating its own witness could select class 1 to match real bytes 0x18 0x1A (digestID 26) while exposing 0x0ABBCC1A -- defeating the digestID-to-claim-bytes binding r6 was meant to establish. Fixed by constraining every value byte the selected class does not encode to zero, per-class, with a regression test that tampers with the witness directly (verified to fail without the fix). Likely fail-safe rather than forgeable (a conformant verifier rejects), but it broke the intended guarantee.
